headline: Plan Bathhouse and Camping Stays Ahead of Arrival
reservation: While the park has no entry fee, camping at Gulpha Gorge requires an official reservation via the Recreation.gov system. Historic bathhouse services are managed by individual private concessionaires; check their specific booking portals for availability as walk-ins are not guaranteed. Always verify current operating hours and system updates on the official NPS website.

days.title: Historic Bathhouse Row and Thermal Origins

stops.name: Fordyce Bathhouse
stops.detail: Visit the park's museum and visitor center to understand the plumbing and social history of the thermal springs.

stops.name: Grand Promenade
stops.detail: Walk this elevated brick path behind the bathhouses for a view of the architecture and natural spring openings.

days.driving: Minimal driving; allow for slow downtown traffic and designated garage parking
days.note: Paved paths can be slick during spring rains; wear appropriate footwear.

days.title: Mountain Vistas and Forest Canopy
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from North Mountain Drive

stops.name: Hot Springs Mountain Tower
stops.detail: Gain an elevated perspective of the Ouachita Mountains and the surrounding valley floor.

stops.name: Peak Trail
stops.detail: A steady uphill route connecting the downtown historic district to the wooded mountain summit.

days.driving: Allow 20-30 minutes for winding mountain roads; conditions vary with weather
days.note: Scenic drives may close during rare winter weather events or maintenance.

days.title: Creek Scenery and West Mountain Hikes

stops.name: Gulpha Gorge Trail
stops.detail: Explore the creek-side scenery and rocky terrain in a quieter section of the park.

stops.name: West Mountain Overlook
stops.detail: Drive or hike to these viewpoints for a different angle of the city and the Ouachita range.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes between Gulpha Gorge and the West Mountain summit
days.note: Summer humidity is high; prioritize outdoor activities before the midday heat.

intel.title: Downtown and Trailhead Spaces
intel.text: Use the free public parking garage on Exchange Street for Bathhouse Row access. Trailhead lots at Gulpha Gorge and mountain overlooks are limited and fill quickly on weekends.

intel.title: Connectivity in the Hollows
intel.text: Cellular service is generally strong downtown but can drop in deep wooded ravines. Download trail maps before leaving the central corridor.

intel.title: Gateway City Supplies
intel.text: Full services are available throughout the city of Hot Springs surrounding the park. Check vehicle range before beginning the scenic mountain loops.

intel.title: Avoiding the Peak
intel.text: Bathhouse Row is busiest during spring break and fall weekends. Mid-week visits offer a more relaxed pace for museum tours.

intel.title: Road and Path Surfaces
intel.text: Mountain roads are narrow with sharp turns; check rental restrictions for large RVs. The Grand Promenade is accessible, but mountain trails involve steep grades.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Memorial Field Airport and drive 7 minutes to central Hot Springs to check in and secure parking before exploring Bathhouse Row.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are ideal for city parking and winding mountain roads; check RV length restrictions for North Mountain Drive.
plan.goldenHour: West Mountain Overlook provides a scenic sunset view, though exact light quality depends on seasonal cloud cover.
